(2) THE DEADLINE LAW, SHIPPED (gait_controller.hpp, hind_alt_due + the fire block): the alternation fire deadline becomes min(the other's last_td + kFoldBudgetTicks - tair - g (the wave-29 fold-budget form, unchanged), THE STANDING LEG'S OWN UNLOAD BOUND), where the unload bound is the DERIVED +1 class (kUnloadTicks = 1, the mined law above) minus the machinery's own hand-off g=1 -- i.e. the unload bound reads the OTHER'S BAND ENTRY TICK ITSELF: the fire must PRECEDE the unload, and the unload is at entry+1, so the window is exactly the entry tick. THE UNLOAD TERM ARMS ONLY IN THE RIDE ERA (hind_step_last_td_[hl] != 0: this leg has completed at least one step-replant) -- the mined control era is the arming's own basis; disarmed, the deadline is the wave-29 fold form EXACTLY, which preserves the whole fence calendar (the L's 108..141 due arithmetic and its 142 deadline fire are byte-identical: the L had completed no replant through 142). The concentration clause flips '<=' to '<' -- the EXCHANGE's own signature (the other's fire on the same tick as this leg's landing) concentrates the ride; byte-identical through 159 (both legs' equal-case never arises before 160). THE HAND-OFF CLAUSE (b) YIELDS TO THE DEADLINE FIRE (new, counted): the wave-29 letter '(a)/(b) NEVER yield' held because the fold deadline (+35) never collides with (b)'s one-tick window -- provably inert there still; the armed unload deadline IS the entry tick, the very tick (b) guards, so (b)'s guard would consume the whole window the law exists to spend.
